title: Binary Black Holes population synthesis based on the current LVK observations
comment: 21 pages, 14 figures, 4 tables
summary: The ongoing observations from ground based gravitational-wave observatories have led to the detection of more than a hundred merger events between black holes. We use the LIGO-Virgo-KAGRA (LVK) observations from 2015 to early 2024, to test the population synthesis of these merging binaries; which will allow us to probe the formation mechanisms and environments of these black holes. We test if the current sample of binary black holes can be explained only by the merger of black holes coming from the collapse of the cores of massive stars, i.e. as just first generation black holes merging with each other. Those black holes' masses will roughly follow a power-law distribution. We also test if in addition to the merger between first generation black holes, there is evidence for a second population of black hole binaries in which at least one the binaries' members is the product of an earlier merger between black holes. These binaries are typically referred to as signals of hierarchical mergers. Such a population can possibly explain the observation of very massive black hole binaries by the LVK collaboration. We find that the LVK observations give a statistical preference in log-likelihood of up to $- 2 Δln\mathcal{L} = -150$ or in log-Bayes factor of up to $ln\textrm{BF} = 71$, for the full sample of black hole binaries originating from a combination of black holes following a power-law distribution and black holes from hierarchical mergers. The ratio of black holes following a power-law mass-distribution to a mass-distribution expected from hierarchical mergers is found to be as high as one-to-one. We also consider that some of the LVK black hole merging binaries are the result of primordial black holes (PBHs), merging inside dark matter halos and in the intergalactic medium. Adding a third population is preferred. [abridged]

AI.tldr: The LVK gravitational-wave data shows strong statistical preference for a mixed population of binary black holes: both first-generation (power-law mass distribution) and hierarchical mergers (products of earlier mergers), with evidence suggesting a 1:1 ratio, and potential inclusion of primordial black holes.
AI.motivation: To test formation mechanisms of merging binary black holes detected by LVK observatories, specifically whether the observed population can be explained solely by first-generation black holes from massive star collapse, or if hierarchical mergers (where at least one black hole results from previous mergers) are needed to explain massive binaries.
AI.method: Analyzed LVK observations from 2015 to early 2024 using statistical population synthesis. Tested three scenarios: 1) only first-generation black holes with power-law mass distribution, 2) combination of first-generation and hierarchical mergers, 3) inclusion of primordial black holes as a third population. Used likelihood ratio tests and Bayesian evidence comparison.
AI.result: Strong statistical preference for mixed population: -2ΔlnL = -150 and lnBF = 71 favoring combination of power-law and hierarchical merger populations. Ratio of power-law to hierarchical merger black holes approximately 1:1. Adding primordial black holes as third population is also statistically preferred.
AI.conclusion: LVK observations cannot be explained solely by first-generation black holes from massive star collapse. Hierarchical mergers constitute a significant fraction (~50%) of the observed binary black hole population, with evidence for additional primordial black hole contribution, revealing complex formation channels.

title: Detecting Axion-like particles using Cosmic Variance Cancellation with CMB and Radio surveys
comment: 39 pages, 12 figures, 5 tables. To be submitted to JCAP
summary: Axions and axion-like particles (ALPs) arise naturally in many extensions of the Standard Model and are among the well-motivated candidates for dark matter. In the presence of magnetic fields of galaxy clusters, Cosmic Microwave Background (CMB) photons can convert to ALPs, with the efficiency of the process governed by the cluster electron density and magnetic field profiles, the photon--ALP coupling strength ($g_{aγ}$), as well as the frequency ($ν$) of the photon at the redshift of the cluster. The CMB blackbody spectrum suggests that this resonant conversion also takes place at radio wavelengths, following the spectral behaviour of the ALP distortion signal. This opens a new window to search for ALPs using cosmic variance cancellation (CVC), with multi-frequency tracers of the same phenomenon in CMB photon--ALP resonant conversion. The constraints on the ALP signal ratios from different combinations of microwave and radio bands of the Simons Observatory (SO) and the Square Kilometre Array (SKA) can be significantly improved using CVC compared to the case of using auto-only spectra from the two experiments. With the large number of galaxy clusters that will be observed by SO and SKA, we will be able to obtain much more information using CVC, especially for low-mass ALPs with stronger signals. Using the auto-only spectra from galaxy clusters up to redshift $z = 1$ for inference of the normalized ratio parameter, we obtain a standard deviation of $5.9 \times 10^{-2}$ for an ALP mass $m_a = 10^{-14} \, \mathrm{eV}$, which improves to $1 \times 10^{-2}$ using CVC. This method provides a universal probe of the ALP distortion signal using its spectral dependence and can also invalidate false detections of the ALP signal based on its frequency behaviour in different bands.

AI.tldr: The paper proposes using cosmic variance cancellation with multi-frequency CMB and radio observations from Simons Observatory and SKA to detect axion-like particles through resonant photon-ALP conversion in galaxy cluster magnetic fields.
AI.motivation: Axions and ALPs are well-motivated dark matter candidates, and their detection through photon-ALP conversion in galaxy clusters provides a promising search method. Current constraints can be improved by leveraging the spectral dependence of the ALP distortion signal across different frequency bands.
AI.method: Uses cosmic variance cancellation (CVC) technique with multi-frequency observations from Simons Observatory (microwave) and Square Kilometre Array (radio) to trace the same photon-ALP resonant conversion phenomenon in galaxy clusters. Analyzes spectral behavior of ALP distortion signal across different frequency bands.
AI.result: CVC significantly improves constraints on ALP signal ratios compared to auto-only spectra analysis. For ALP mass m_a = 10^{-14} eV, standard deviation improves from 5.9×10^{-2} (auto-only) to 1×10^{-2} (with CVC). The method is particularly effective for low-mass ALPs with stronger signals.
AI.conclusion: CVC with multi-frequency SO and SKA observations provides a powerful universal probe for ALP detection using spectral dependence, enabling improved constraints and validation of potential detections through frequency behavior analysis across different bands.

title: Statistical consistency of sign-switching vacuum energy with cosmological observations
comment: 15 pages, 8 figures
summary: We assess dataset agreement and late-time predictive adequacy in $Λ$CDM and its sign-switching extension, $Λ_{\rm s}$CDM, using a suite of Gaussian and exact non-Gaussian consistency diagnostics. Both models are constrained with cosmic microwave background measurements from Planck, ACT, and SPT, baryon acoustic oscillation data from DESI DR2, and low-redshift Type Ia supernova data from PantheonPlus+SH0ES. We find that commonly used Gaussian tension metrics can significantly overstate inconsistencies when broad, non-Gaussian posteriors are combined with tightly constrained datasets. In contrast, the exact non-Gaussian parameter shift indicates excellent consistency between CMB and BAO observations in both models. The $Λ_{\rm s}$CDM extension modestly improves geometric compatibility at intermediate redshifts, although reductions in parameter-level tension do not necessarily imply improved predictive consistency. These results highlight the importance of exact, non-Gaussian, and predictive diagnostics for robust assessments of cosmological model consistency.

AI.tldr: The paper analyzes dataset agreement and predictive adequacy in ΛCDM and its sign-switching extension ΛsCDM, finding that Gaussian tension metrics can overstate inconsistencies with non-Gaussian posteriors, while exact non-Gaussian diagnostics show good consistency between CMB and BAO data.
AI.motivation: To assess dataset agreement and late-time predictive adequacy in standard ΛCDM cosmology and its sign-switching extension ΛsCDM, addressing concerns about potential inconsistencies between cosmological datasets and the limitations of commonly used Gaussian tension metrics.
AI.method: Uses a suite of Gaussian and exact non-Gaussian consistency diagnostics applied to both ΛCDM and ΛsCDM models. Constraints are derived from Planck, ACT, and SPT CMB measurements, DESI DR2 BAO data, and PantheonPlus+SH0ES Type Ia supernova data.
AI.result: Gaussian tension metrics significantly overstate inconsistencies when broad non-Gaussian posteriors combine with tightly constrained datasets. Exact non-Gaussian parameter shift shows excellent consistency between CMB and BAO observations in both models. ΛsCDM modestly improves geometric compatibility at intermediate redshifts, but reduced parameter-level tension doesn't necessarily imply improved predictive consistency.
AI.conclusion: Exact, non-Gaussian, and predictive diagnostics are crucial for robust assessments of cosmological model consistency, as conventional Gaussian metrics can be misleading when dealing with non-Gaussian posterior distributions.

title: Constraints on Neutrino Mass with Void Weak Lensing Effect
comment: 14 pages, 11 figures, submitted to PRD
summary: Cosmic voids, the underdense regions of the Large Scale Structure (LSS), provide cosmological information highly complementary to that obtained from overdense regions. In this work, we investigate the constraining power of the void-shear cross-correlation (void lensing effect) on the total neutrino mass. Based on cosmological simulations with varying neutrino masses, we identify voids with the DIVE void finder and obtain their density profiles from the underlying dark matter and neutrino distributions. We then generate mock shear catalogues through ray-tracing and measure the corresponding void lensing signals. Our results show that void lensing yields an independent constraint on total neutrino mass as $σ(M_ν)=0.096\,{\rm eV}$ in the absence of shape noise, and $σ(M_ν)=0.340\,{\rm eV}$ when adopting a Stage-III-like shape noise ($σ_e \simeq 0.3$). Moreover, we find a clear linear relationship between the void lensing signal and neutrino mass. We further validate the forward modelling of the void lensing signal from the void density profiles across different cosmologies, demonstrating its accuracy and potential for future applications. These findings highlight void lensing as a promising probe of massive neutrinos and motivate its applications to galaxy survey data as well as the combination with other cosmological observables.

AI.tldr: Void-shear cross-correlation (void lensing) provides competitive constraints on total neutrino mass, with σ(M_ν)=0.096 eV (no noise) and 0.340 eV (Stage-III-like noise), showing linear relationship with neutrino mass.
AI.motivation: Cosmic voids offer complementary cosmological information to overdense regions. The void-shear cross-correlation (void lensing effect) can constrain total neutrino mass, which is important for understanding fundamental particle physics and cosmology.
AI.method: Used cosmological simulations with varying neutrino masses, identified voids with DIVE void finder, obtained density profiles from dark matter and neutrino distributions, generated mock shear catalogues through ray-tracing, measured void lensing signals, and validated forward modelling across different cosmologies.
AI.result: Void lensing yields independent constraints: σ(M_ν)=0.096 eV without shape noise and σ(M_ν)=0.340 eV with Stage-III-like shape noise (σ_e ≈ 0.3). Found clear linear relationship between void lensing signal and neutrino mass. Forward modelling validation shows accuracy across different cosmologies.
AI.conclusion: Void lensing is a promising probe of massive neutrinos, motivating applications to galaxy survey data and combination with other cosmological observables for improved constraints on neutrino mass.

title: Quantifying the Milky Way, LMC and their interaction using all-sky kinematics of outer halo stars
comment: MNRAS submitted. 17 pages, 12 figures, 2 tables. arXiv admin note: text overlap with arXiv:2510.04735
summary: The recent pericentric passage of the Large Magellanic Cloud (LMC) through the Milky Way (MW) has dislodged its centre of mass, inducing a state of dynamical disequilibrium, the reflex motion, in the kinematics of outer stellar halo stars. Using data out to distances of $160 \, \rm kpc$ from the combined H3+SEGUE+MagE outer halo survey, we constrain the mass of the MW and LMC, as well as the resulting reflex motion and the velocity anisotropy of the stellar halo. Using a suite of 32,000 rigid MW--LMC simulations, each with a MW stellar halo evolved to the present day in the combined MW--LMC potential, we perform Simulation Based Inference by training a neural posterior estimator on the means and dispersions of the radial and tangential velocities of stars from the combined H3+SEGUE+MagE outer halo sample. Relative to halo stars at $100 \, \rm kpc$, we find the magnitude of the reflex velocity to be $v_{\rm travel} = 39.4^{+7.6}_{-7.2}\,\rm km \, s^{-1}$. Simultaneously, we determine the enclosed MW mass to be $M_{\rm MW}(< 50 \, \rm kpc) = 3.63 \pm 0.16 \times 10^{11}\, \rm M_{\odot}$ and the enclosed LMC mass to be $M_{\rm LMC}(< 50 \, \rm kpc) = 9.74^{+2.07}_{-1.81} \times 10^{10}\, \rm M_{\odot}$. Our results suggest that the total LMC mass must be at least $\sim20\%$ that of the MW. The velocity anisotropy prior to the LMC's infall is constrained to be $β_0 = 0.61 \pm 0.03$. Finally, we demonstrate that failing to account for the LMC in models biases the MW mass estimate to prefer slightly more massive values.

AI.tldr: Using outer halo stellar kinematics data and simulations, researchers measured Milky Way and Large Magellanic Cloud masses, finding the LMC's recent passage induces a 39.4 km/s reflex motion in halo stars and that the LMC mass is at least 20% of the MW's mass.
AI.motivation: The recent pericentric passage of the Large Magellanic Cloud through the Milky Way has disrupted the equilibrium of outer halo stars, creating reflex motion. This provides an opportunity to constrain both the MW and LMC masses using stellar kinematics, but existing models often neglect the LMC's influence, potentially biasing mass estimates.
AI.method: Used combined H3+SEGUE+MagE outer halo survey data out to 160 kpc distances. Performed 32,000 rigid MW-LMC simulations with evolved stellar halos in the combined potential. Applied Simulation Based Inference by training a neural posterior estimator on radial and tangential velocity means and dispersions from the observational data.
AI.result: Found reflex velocity magnitude of 39.4 km/s relative to halo stars at 100 kpc. Determined enclosed MW mass within 50 kpc: 3.63±0.16×10¹¹ M⊙. Enclosed LMC mass within 50 kpc: 9.74⁺²·⁰⁷₋₁·⁸¹×10¹⁰ M⊙. Velocity anisotropy prior to LMC infall: β₀=0.61±0.03. Results indicate total LMC mass must be at least ~20% of MW mass.
AI.conclusion: The LMC's influence on Milky Way halo kinematics is significant and must be accounted for in mass modeling. Failing to include the LMC in models biases MW mass estimates toward higher values. The LMC is a substantial satellite with mass at least 20% of the MW, making it a major perturber in the Local Group.

title: Mock Catalogs of Strongly Lensed Gravitational Waves via A Halo Model Approach with Ground-based Detectors
comment: 23 pages, 12 figures, 5 tables
summary: As plans for the construction of third-generation gravitational wave (GW) detectors advance, research into strongly lensed GWs has become increasingly critical. It is anticipated that hundreds of multi-image lensed GWs will be detected annually. We present a comprehensive suite of lensed GW mock catalog derived from a composite lens mass model incorporating dark matter halos, galaxies, and subhalos. We analyze three source populations with four detector network configurations considering the earth rotation. Our simulations encompass not only conventional doublets and quadruplets but also subhalo-lensed events, highly magnified systems, and complete three or five image systems with a detectable central image, a feature distinct from optical lensing. For the joint ET+CE network, we forecast an annual detection rate of approximately 400 doublets and 36 quadruplets. Notably, this population includes roughly 107 events lensed by subhalos and 20 complete systems with detectable central images. Furthermore, we analyze high-magnification events ($μ> 3$), predicting approximately 360 such cases. Under a more relaxed selection criterion that requires only at least one lensed signal to exceed the detection threshold, we estimate a total of approximately 617 lensed events. We also investigate the impact of variations in lens mass models and stellar evolution models on event rates, as well as the distributions of SNR pairs and time delays. These results establish a more physically grounded statistical prior for the future identification and authentication of lensed GW signals. The Gravitational Waves-Lensing Mock Catalog (GW-LMC) have been made publicly available.

AI.tldr: Researchers create a comprehensive mock catalog of lensed gravitational waves for third-generation detectors, predicting ~400 doublets and ~36 quadruplets annually for ET+CE network, including subhalo-lensed events and systems with detectable central images.
AI.motivation: With third-generation gravitational wave detectors being planned, there's a critical need to understand strongly lensed GW signals. Hundreds of multi-image lensed GWs are expected annually, requiring comprehensive simulations to establish statistical priors for future identification and authentication of these signals.
AI.method: Developed a comprehensive lensed GW mock catalog using a composite lens mass model incorporating dark matter halos, galaxies, and subhalos. Analyzed three source populations with four detector network configurations considering Earth's rotation. Simulations included conventional doublets/quadruplets, subhalo-lensed events, highly magnified systems, and complete systems with detectable central images.
AI.result: For ET+CE network: ~400 doublets and ~36 quadruplets annually, including ~107 subhalo-lensed events and ~20 complete systems with detectable central images. ~360 high-magnification events (μ>3). Under relaxed criteria: ~617 total lensed events. Investigated impacts of lens mass models and stellar evolution on rates, plus SNR pairs and time delay distributions.
AI.conclusion: The study establishes physically grounded statistical priors for future identification of lensed GW signals and makes the Gravitational Waves-Lensing Mock Catalog (GW-LMC) publicly available, providing crucial tools for third-generation detector research.

title: Reliable Tests of Faint-end UV Luminosity Functions in Strong Lensing Fields
comment: PhD Thesis
summary: Dark matter comprises ~85% of the entire mass of the Universe, but the fundamental nature of its constituent particles remains elusive. In this thesis, I test for two competitive dark matter models: the conventional heavy particle paradigm, and dark matter being ultralight bosons of mass $\sim 10^{-22}$eV ($ψ$DM). More specifically, I test for the faint-end turnover induced by $ψ$DM models, exploiting the strong lensing power by massive galaxy clusters to probe intrinsically fainter magnitudes. A key challenge for such an analysis would be contamination by low-z galaxies sharing similar observed SEDs as high-z galaxies. As I will demonstrate, such a contamination issue is generally severe and may wash out the faint-end turnover signatures. I also show that $\sim 50\%$ of the purported $3.5\leq z\leq 5.5$ galaxies within existing photometric redshift catalogs constructed for Hubble Frontier Fields (HFF) are in fact low-z interlopers. Luckily, individual mitigation of interlopers can be achieved with the combination of deep HST and JWST observations. For fields without supplementary data, machine learning methods will be shown useful in preserving the mitigating power. Cleaner $3.5\leq z\leq 5.5$ and $6\leq z\leq 10$ samples are derived for a more reliable test in strong lensing field of MACS J0416, with which I found no evidence for faint-end turnovers, leading to a constraint on the $ψ$DM mass of $>2.97\times10^{-22}$eV at 95\% confidence. This constraint will also be interpreted in an scheme where dark matter is composed of multiple particle copies, where I argue the derived mass bound is likely on an effective de Broglie scale governing the collective behavior of the entire $ψ$DM budget under gravitational equilibrium established.

AI.tldr: Thesis tests dark matter models using strong lensing to probe faint galaxy populations, finds no evidence for ultralight boson dark matter-induced faint-end turnover, constrains ψDM mass >2.97×10⁻²²eV.
AI.motivation: To test competing dark matter models: conventional heavy particles vs. ultralight bosons (ψDM) by examining faint-end galaxy luminosity function turnover predicted by ψDM models, using strong lensing to probe intrinsically faint galaxies.
AI.method: Uses strong lensing by massive galaxy clusters (MACS J0416) to probe intrinsically faint galaxies; addresses contamination from low-z interlopers through deep HST+JWST observations and machine learning methods; derives cleaner 3.5≤z≤5.5 and 6≤z≤10 galaxy samples for analysis.
AI.result: Found ~50% of purported 3.5≤z≤5.5 galaxies in Hubble Frontier Fields photometric redshift catalogs are low-z interlopers; after cleaning samples, found no evidence for faint-end turnover, constraining ψDM mass >2.97×10⁻²²eV at 95% confidence.
AI.conclusion: No evidence supports ψDM-induced faint-end turnover; constraint represents lower bound on effective de Broglie scale governing collective behavior of ψDM under gravitational equilibrium in multi-particle scenario.

title: Recovering the infall mass for Milky Way satellite galaxy Sextans
comment: 16 pages, 9 figures, accepted for publication in MNRAS
summary: Understanding the formation and evolution of the Milky Way (MW) requires detailed knowledge of its satellite galaxies. In this study, we focus on the Sextans dwarf spheroidal (dSph) galaxy, a faint, dark matter (DM)-dominated satellite, to investigate the role of tidal and baryonic effects in shaping its observed properties. Using tailored $N$-body simulations, we explore possible orbits of Sextans in different MW models to reconstruct its progenitor's properties. Our simulations demonstrate the stars in Sextans are only mildly affected by galactic tides and the stellar kinematics provide robust constraints on its dynamical mass within the half-light radius, while the tidal mass loss of its DM component depends primarily on MW mass. The recovered infall mass of Sextans ranges from $1.22$ to $3.14\times10^9\rm\,M_\odot$ for MW masses from $0.8$ to $2\times10^{12}\rm\,M_\odot$. If the DM density remained as cuspy as NFW profile, the infall mass would be smaller by a factor of 2. Although with large ranges, the possible infall masses of Sextans recovered by our simulations are consistent with the stellar mass-halo mass relation in TNG50 and abundance matching results. We find some cases for the cuspy DM density profile where the infall mass is smaller than $10^9\rm\,M_\odot$, possibly indicating that star formation in Sextans is more efficient than in other satellites. The recovered DM halo structural parameters from our simulations provide valuable constraints for future studies on the DM content and formation history of Sextans.

AI.tldr: N-body simulations of Sextans dwarf spheroidal galaxy reveal its infall mass ranges from 1.22-3.14×10⁹ M☉ depending on Milky Way mass, with stellar kinematics providing robust dynamical mass constraints while DM tidal stripping depends primarily on MW mass.
AI.motivation: To understand the formation and evolution of the Milky Way by studying its satellite galaxies, specifically investigating how tidal and baryonic effects shape the observed properties of the Sextans dwarf spheroidal galaxy.
AI.method: Used tailored N-body simulations to explore possible orbits of Sextans in different Milky Way models, reconstructing progenitor properties and analyzing effects of galactic tides on stars and dark matter.
AI.result: Stars in Sextans are only mildly affected by tides, with stellar kinematics providing robust constraints on dynamical mass within half-light radius. Infall mass ranges from 1.22-3.14×10⁹ M☉ for MW masses of 0.8-2×10¹² M☉. Cuspy NFW profiles yield smaller infall masses by factor of 2, with some cases below 10⁹ M☉ suggesting potentially more efficient star formation.
AI.conclusion: Recovered infall masses are consistent with stellar mass-halo mass relations from TNG50 and abundance matching. The simulations provide valuable constraints on dark matter halo structural parameters for future studies of Sextans' dark matter content and formation history.

title: Hidden Vela Supercluster Revealed by First Hybrid Redshift & Peculiar Velocity Reconstruction
comment: Submitted to A&A : aa59752-26
summary:
A large fraction of the extragalactic sky is obscured by foreground dust and stars along the plane of the Milky Way, leaving a major gap (~ 20%) in whole-sky maps of large-scale structures -- an incompleteness that is even more severe for peculiar velocity samples. This has long limited an unambiguous interpretation of observed cosmic flows and their connection to the underlying mass-density field.
  We present a new hybrid reconstruction methodology which combines 65,518 galaxy peculiar velocity distances from the CF4++ catalogue (Courtois2025) with 8283 new galaxy redshifts observed near the southern Galactic plane (|b| <= 10 degrees) Zone of Avoidance. A major advance is the inclusion of 2176 high-sensitivity, interferometric HI redshifts obtained with the SARAO MeerKAT telescope which for the first time provide coverage of the innermost 3degrees-wide strip of the southern ZOA and to unprecedented depth.
  This hybrid redshifts & peculiar velocities approach yields a substantially revised view of the inferred overdensities in and around the ZOA. In particular, the Vela supercluster emerges as a dominant mass concentration, rivaling the Shapley concentration and exceeding the mass associated with Laniakea and the Great Attractor region. With a total mass of 33.8 10^16 Msol, a characteristic radius of 70 hmpc, and a double core morphology at a distance of 189 hmpc, Vela dominates the mass budget and gravitational influence of the southern Zone of Avoidance. These results provide the most complete and dynamically consistent picture to date of the southern Zone of Avoidance and demonstrate the transformative potential of hybrid reconstruction techniques tailored for the next generation of large-scale surveys.

AI.tldr: New hybrid reconstruction method combines peculiar velocities with new redshift data from the southern Galactic plane Zone of Avoidance, revealing the Vela supercluster as a dominant mass concentration rivaling Shapley and exceeding Laniakea/Great Attractor.
AI.motivation: The Milky Way's dust and stars obscure ~20% of the extragalactic sky, creating a major gap in whole-sky maps of large-scale structures and limiting interpretation of cosmic flows and their connection to the underlying mass-density field, particularly for peculiar velocity samples.
AI.method: Hybrid reconstruction methodology combining 65,518 galaxy peculiar velocity distances from CF4++ catalogue with 8,283 new galaxy redshifts observed near the southern Galactic plane Zone of Avoidance (|b| ≤ 10°), including 2,176 high-sensitivity interferometric HI redshifts from SARAO MeerKAT telescope covering the innermost 3°-wide strip.
AI.result: Vela supercluster emerges as dominant mass concentration with total mass of 33.8 × 10¹⁶ M☉, characteristic radius of 70 h⁻¹ Mpc, double core morphology at distance of 189 h⁻¹ Mpc, rivaling Shapley concentration and exceeding mass associated with Laniakea and Great Attractor region.
AI.conclusion: The hybrid redshifts & peculiar velocities approach provides the most complete and dynamically consistent picture to date of the southern Zone of Avoidance and demonstrates transformative potential of hybrid reconstruction techniques for next-generation large-scale surveys.

title: Electron densities and filling factors of extragalactic HII regions: NGC 2403 and NGC 628
comment: 22 pages, 16 figures. Accepted for publication in MNRAS
summary: Measurements of the electron density of populations of extragalactic HII regions in nearby galaxies remain limited, despite the relevance of this quantity for characterizing the porosity of the interstellar medium and the escape of the ionizing radiation. We initiated a project aimed at analyzing the root-mean-square electron density ne_rms, the in-situ density ne and the volume filling factor (phi) of extragalactic HII regions, investigating the dependence of these attributes on nebular and host galaxy properties. We present an image-segmentation methodology for constructing homogeneous HII region catalogues, and apply it to two pilot galaxies: NGC 2403 and NGC 628. We derive ne_rms from their Halpha luminosities and equivalent radii (R_eq), and obtain ne and phi for spectroscopic subsamples. While ne is below 300 cm$^{-3}$, ne_rms is typically one to two orders of magnitude lower, implying that phi is in the range ~$10^{-4}$ to $10^{-1}$. The two galaxies exhibit a similar size-density relation, which breaks for R_eq >~ 50 pc, show at most a weak dependence of ne_rms on galactocentric radius for NGC 2403, and no clear dependence of ne or phi on these parameters. Combining these results with published data, ne_rms presents tentative scaling relations with the median HII region size, the fraction of large regions in the parent galaxy, and the star formation rate surface density. These trends, if confirmed, would provide new constraints for massive cluster formation models and important clues for interpreting dependencies observed at high redshift, underscoring the necessity of consistently extending this analysis to larger samples.

AI.tldr: This paper presents a methodology for analyzing electron density properties of extragalactic HII regions in nearby galaxies, focusing on root-mean-square density (ne_rms), in-situ density (ne), and volume filling factor (phi), with applications to NGC 2403 and NGC 628.
AI.motivation: Measurements of electron density in extragalactic HII regions remain limited despite their importance for characterizing interstellar medium porosity and ionizing radiation escape. There's a need to investigate how these density attributes depend on nebular and host galaxy properties.
AI.method: Developed an image-segmentation methodology for constructing homogeneous HII region catalogues. Applied to two pilot galaxies (NGC 2403 and NGC 628). Derived ne_rms from Hα luminosities and equivalent radii (R_eq), and obtained ne and phi for spectroscopic subsamples. Combined results with published data to identify scaling relations.
AI.result: ne is below 300 cm⁻³, while ne_rms is typically 1-2 orders of magnitude lower, implying phi in range ~10⁻⁴ to 10⁻¹. Both galaxies show similar size-density relations that break for R_eq ≳ 50 pc. Weak dependence of ne_rms on galactocentric radius for NGC 2403, no clear dependence of ne or phi on these parameters. Tentative scaling relations identified between ne_rms and median HII region size, fraction of large regions, and star formation rate surface density.
AI.conclusion: The identified trends, if confirmed, would provide new constraints for massive cluster formation models and important clues for interpreting high-redshift dependencies. The work underscores the necessity of consistently extending this analysis to larger samples to validate and refine these findings.

title: Pure Natural Inflation Passes the ACT
comment: 6 Pages, 6 Figures
summary: Pure natural inflation is a compelling effectively single-field model of inflation stemming from a top-down approach to the acceleration mechanism. In this short letter we show that such model is compatible with the latest CMB constraints from the Atacama Cosmology Telescope. Under both the instantaneous reheating hypothesis and standard assumptions for reheating, we rule in a non-trivial fraction of the parameter space. We apply our analysis also to a phenomenological extension of the model and chart its viable parameter space.

AI.tldr: Pure natural inflation remains viable under latest CMB constraints from ACT, with non-trivial parameter space surviving both instantaneous and standard reheating assumptions.
AI.motivation: To demonstrate that pure natural inflation, a top-down motivated single-field model, remains compatible with the latest CMB constraints from the Atacama Cosmology Telescope (ACT).
AI.method: Analysis of pure natural inflation under both instantaneous reheating hypothesis and standard reheating assumptions, applying constraints from ACT CMB data, and extending the analysis to a phenomenological extension of the model.
AI.result: Pure natural inflation is ruled in with a non-trivial fraction of parameter space surviving constraints. The phenomenological extension also shows viable parameter space regions.
AI.conclusion: Pure natural inflation remains a viable inflationary model despite stringent CMB constraints, with both the original model and its phenomenological extension having non-trivial viable parameter space.

title: Winding, Unwinding, Rewinding the Gaia Phase Spiral
comment: 8 pages, 1 figure, conference summary submitted to PASP
summary: The Gaia Space Satellite has transformed the field of Galactic Dynamics by collecting 6D phase space information for hundreds of millions of stars. In 2018, it enabled the discovery of the Gaia Phase Spiral (Antoja et al., 2018), a clear signal in the vertical motion of the stars that reveals how far from equilibrium the Galactic disk is. Seven years after the discovery of this structure, a workshop dedicated to the Phase Spiral took place at the Lorentz Center. Workshop participants summarized the current state of knowledge about the Phase Spiral and identified open questions and key areas to continue progressing in understanding the origin of the Phase Spiral and the physics governing the response of the disk to perturbations. Here, we aim to summarize the content and discussions of this workshop, share the resources that have been produced at this workshop with the broader community, and invite interested individuals to join on the projects that started.

AI.tldr: Workshop summary on the Gaia Phase Spiral, covering current knowledge, open questions, and future research directions for understanding this Galactic disk perturbation signal discovered in Gaia data.
AI.motivation: To document and disseminate the discussions, findings, and resources from the Lorentz Center workshop on the Gaia Phase Spiral, which was organized seven years after its discovery to assess current understanding and identify future research directions.
AI.method: Workshop organization and synthesis of expert discussions from the Lorentz Center meeting, including compilation of current knowledge, identification of open questions, and creation of community resources.
AI.result: Comprehensive summary of the workshop proceedings, including state-of-the-art understanding of the Phase Spiral, key unresolved questions about its origin and disk physics, and available resources for the broader astronomical community.
AI.conclusion: The workshop successfully consolidated current knowledge about the Gaia Phase Spiral, identified critical research gaps, and established collaborative projects and resources to advance understanding of Galactic disk dynamics and perturbation responses.

title: Exploring the $S_8$ Tension: Insights from the CatNorth 1.5-Million Quasar Candidates
comment: 24 pages, 21 figures, 2 tables, accepted by APJ
summary: The parameter $S_8$, a key probe of cosmic structure growth, exhibits a persistent $\sim3σ$ tension between high-redshift measurements from cosmic microwave background (CMB) anisotropies and low-redshift weak gravitational lensing observations. This discrepancy may indicate either unaccounted systematic effects or new physics beyond the standard $Λ$CDM cosmology. In this work, we constrain $S_8$ using the high purity CatNorth 1.5 million quasar candidate catalog and the {\it Planck} DR4 CMB lensing data across the broad redshift ranges through auto-correlation and cross-correlation analyses. To address the spatial incompleteness, we develop a machine-learning-based selection function that effectively suppresses the systematics-induced power spectrum excess on large scales. Our robust low-redshift measurements at $z<1.5$ yield $S_8 = 0.844^{+0.058}_{-0.056}$, consistent with the {\it Planck} 2018 CMB anisotropies constraints of $S_8=0.834\pm0.016$ but lower than the $0.879^{+0.055}_{-0.055}$ reported by a previous work using the Quaia quasar candidate catalog. However, for high-redshift faint quasars at $z>1.5$, we find a lower value of $S_8=0.724^{+0.058}_{-0.054}$, likely due to the sample incompleteness and/or the foreground contamination. Further tests on the volume-limited samples exhibit a consistent trend: $S_8 = 0.835^{+0.053}_{-0.049}$ for $z < 2$, $0.824^{+0.061}_{-0.062}$ for $0.4 < z < 1.5$, and a lower value of $0.789^{+0.062}_{-0.062}$ for the higher redshift range of $1.5 < z < 2.5$. While future data may refine these results, our current measurements based on a large sample of quasar candidates show less evidence of the $S_8$ tension.

AI.tldr: Using CatNorth quasar catalog and Planck CMB lensing data, researchers constrain S₈ parameter to resolve tension between high-z CMB and low-z lensing measurements, finding consistency with Planck at low redshifts but lower values at high redshifts.
AI.motivation: Address the persistent ~3σ tension in S₈ parameter between high-redshift CMB measurements and low-redshift weak lensing observations, which could indicate either systematic effects or new physics beyond ΛCDM cosmology.
AI.method: Use CatNorth 1.5 million quasar candidate catalog and Planck DR4 CMB lensing data across broad redshift ranges; perform auto-correlation and cross-correlation analyses; develop machine-learning-based selection function to address spatial incompleteness and suppress systematics-induced power spectrum excess on large scales.
AI.result: Low-redshift (z<1.5) measurements yield S₈ = 0.844⁺⁰·⁰⁵⁸₋₀·₀₅₆, consistent with Planck 2018 CMB constraints (0.834±0.016) but lower than previous Quaia catalog results (0.879⁺⁰·⁰⁵⁵₋₀·₀₅₅). High-redshift (z>1.5) faint quasars show lower S₈=0.724⁺⁰·⁰⁵⁸₋₀·₀₅₄, likely due to sample incompleteness/foreground contamination. Volume-limited samples show consistent trend: S₈ = 0.835⁺⁰·⁰⁵³₋₀·₀₄⁹ (z<2), 0.824⁺⁰·⁰⁶¹₋₀·₀₆² (0.4<z<1.5), and 0.789⁺⁰·⁰⁶²₋₀·₀₆² (1.5<z<2.5).
AI.conclusion: Current measurements based on large quasar candidate sample show less evidence of the S₈ tension, though high-redshift results may be affected by sample incompleteness and foreground contamination; future data may refine these results.

title: HI Observations of Giant Low Surface Brightness Galaxies
comment: Accepted by ApJ
summary: Giant low surface brightness galaxies (gLSBs) are galaxies with extremely extended, faint, optical disks over 50 kpc in radius and have high total masses which can reach 10^12 solar masses. The existence of such galaxies is problematic for current models of galaxy formation, since the major mergers responsible for the large total mass would likely have destroyed the extended optical disk. Examining the gas content of these galaxies is an important step in determining their formation mechanism, whether it be through slow gas accretion or the large disk (re)forming after a major merger. We present neutral atomic hydrogen (HI) observations of 19 gLSBs identified with the Hyper Suprime-Cam Subaru Strategic Program survey. Although most have high HI masses, they are generally lower than expected based on their large optical sizes, and we do identify some gLSBs with unusually low gas content. The HI spectra of these galaxies show evidence for a rotational disk, though these disks are more asymmetric than other galaxies with comparable mass. Four galaxies with similar surface brightness profiles to the gLSBs have also been selected from the Numerical Investigation of a Hundred Astrophysical Objects (NIHAO) simulation for comparison. There is evidence for significant galaxy mergers in the past for three of these NIHAO galaxies and these three galaxies show similar asymmetry in their HI spectra. Together, these results could indicate the large optical disk of gLSBs are the result of a recent merger.

AI.tldr: Giant low surface brightness galaxies (gLSBs) challenge galaxy formation models; HI observations reveal lower-than-expected gas masses and asymmetric disks, suggesting recent mergers may explain their large optical disks.
AI.motivation: gLSBs with extremely extended, faint optical disks (>50 kpc) and high total masses (up to 10^12 M☉) pose problems for current galaxy formation models, as major mergers that could produce such masses would likely destroy extended disks. Understanding their formation mechanism requires examining their gas content to distinguish between slow gas accretion versus disk reformation after mergers.
AI.method: Neutral atomic hydrogen (HI) observations of 19 gLSBs identified from Hyper Suprime-Cam Subaru Strategic Program survey, analyzing HI masses, spectra, and disk asymmetry. Comparison with 4 similar galaxies from NIHAO simulations to examine merger histories and HI spectral properties.
AI.result: Most gLSBs have high HI masses but lower than expected given their large optical sizes, with some showing unusually low gas content. HI spectra indicate rotational disks but with greater asymmetry than comparable-mass galaxies. NIHAO simulations show three of four similar galaxies had significant past mergers and exhibit similar HI spectral asymmetry.
AI.conclusion: The combined observational and simulation evidence suggests gLSBs' large optical disks may result from recent mergers rather than slow gas accretion, explaining both their high masses and extended disk structures.

title: Dark Matter Recoupling
comment: 24 pages + appendices, 9 figures, 1 table
summary: In the late Universe, and on cosmological scales, dark matter is conventionally assumed to be collisionless, as a consequence of the strong existing bounds on dark matter interactions at the Cosmic Microwave Background last-scattering surface. Challenging this lore, here we show that dark matter interactions can be naturally weak at early times, but then grow to observationally relevant strengths at very late times, even significantly after reionization. This is realized if dark matter recouples to a dark radiation species in the range of redshifts probed by the current generation of galaxy surveys. We systematically study, for the first time, the phenomenology of this dark matter recoupling scenario. A combination of Cosmic Microwave Background and Baryon Acoustic Oscillation data show that the interaction needs to be weak at present, if the entirety of dark matter couples to dark radiation. From a complementary perspective, a 4% fraction of dark matter could still be strongly interacting today. Implications for a microscopic model realizing the recoupling dynamics are discussed.

AI.tldr: Dark matter interactions can grow from weak early times to observationally relevant strengths at very late times through recoupling to dark radiation, challenging the conventional assumption of collisionless dark matter.
AI.motivation: To challenge the conventional assumption that dark matter is collisionless on cosmological scales by showing that dark matter interactions can naturally evolve from weak early times to observationally relevant strengths at very late times through recoupling to dark radiation.
AI.method: Systematically study the phenomenology of dark matter recoupling scenario where dark matter recouples to a dark radiation species in the redshift range probed by current galaxy surveys, using Cosmic Microwave Background and Baryon Acoustic Oscillation data.
AI.result: Combined CMB and BAO data show that if the entirety of dark matter couples to dark radiation, the interaction needs to be weak at present. Alternatively, a 4% fraction of dark matter could still be strongly interacting today.
AI.conclusion: Dark matter recoupling to dark radiation provides a viable scenario where interactions evolve from weak early times to potentially observable strengths at late times, with implications for microscopic models realizing this dynamics.

title: Optical QPOs with different periodicities in CSS and ZTF light curves of the quasar 4C 50.43
comment: 4 pages, 3 figures, Accepted to be published in A&A Letters
summary: Long-standing optical quasi-periodic oscillations (QPOs) with periodicity of hundreds to thousands of days have been accepted as indicators for central sub-pc binary black hole systems (BBHs) in broad line active galactic nuclei (BLAGN). However, there are so far no direct reports on whether such reported optical QPOs have their periodicities constant in different periods. Here, based on different methods applied to light curves of 4C 50.43 in different periods, optical QPOs with periodicity of 1124days was detected in the CSS V-band light curve, while a shorter periodicity of 513days was detected in the ZTF g/r band light curves. Despite the two periodicities near-harmonic 2:1 ratio, their absence of simultaneous detection in the lomb-scargle periodograms of the ZTF light curves suggests that they are unlikely to be harmonically related. Potential factors were considered to explain these two distinct periodicities, especially different temporal coverage, signal-to-noise ratio and time steps between the CSS and ZTF light curves, as well as the effects of red noises related to intrinsic AGN variability. Our analysis shows that red noises have strong influence on the different periodicities in 4C 50.43 supporting our previous simulations. The results in this manuscript strongly indicate that it should be cautioned for applications of determined optical QPOs in BLAGN having strong intrinsic AGN variability.

AI.tldr: Optical QPOs in BLAGN 4C 50.43 show different periodicities (1124 days in CSS V-band vs 513 days in ZTF g/r bands) despite near-harmonic 2:1 ratio, suggesting they are not harmonically related and are strongly influenced by red noise from intrinsic AGN variability.
AI.motivation: To investigate whether reported optical quasi-periodic oscillations (QPOs) in broad line active galactic nuclei (BLAGN) maintain constant periodicities over different time periods, challenging the assumption that these QPOs reliably indicate central binary black hole systems.
AI.method: Applied different analysis methods to light curves of 4C 50.43 from different surveys: CSS V-band and ZTF g/r bands. Used Lomb-Scargle periodograms to detect periodicities, considered factors like temporal coverage, signal-to-noise ratio, time steps, and effects of red noise related to intrinsic AGN variability.
AI.result: Detected two distinct periodicities: 1124 days in CSS V-band light curve and 513 days in ZTF g/r band light curves. Despite near-harmonic 2:1 ratio, the periodicities were not simultaneously detected in Lomb-Scargle periodograms, suggesting they are not harmonically related. Red noise from intrinsic AGN variability strongly influenced the different periodicities.
AI.conclusion: Optical QPOs in BLAGN with strong intrinsic AGN variability should be interpreted with caution, as red noise can significantly affect periodicity determinations, potentially leading to spurious or variable periodic signals that may not reliably indicate binary black hole systems.
